chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We were told by Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Ala' al-Arjani, from al-Ala' ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the stingy one is the one who acquires wealth from an unlawful source and spends it in an unjustified manner.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a stingy person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents a nuanced definition of stinginess (bukhl) that transcends mere hoarding, emphasizing the dual failure of illicit acquisition and misappropriation of wealth. This interpretation aligns with Shia juristic discourse, where economic justice is viewed as integral to spiritual purity, linking material conduct directly to moral integrity. The hadith thus serves as a foundational text for understanding the ethical dimensions of wealth management in Islamic economics.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Nadhr bin Suwayd, from Abdul-A’la al-Arjani,from Abdul-A’la bin A’yan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
Indeed, the stingy is the one who acquires a property from other than its lawful method and spends it in other than its right.
